components.name: Installation capsule
components.description: Static illustration of the capsule artwork. Native Finder supplies the interactive files and labels; the SwiftUI renderer is authoritative.
components.css: .ds-installation-capsule { display: grid; place-items: center; width: 574px; height: 194px; border-radius: 97px; background: linear-gradient(#F5F7FA, #E2E7EE); box-shadow: 6px 16px 20px rgba(143,155,177,.28), 0 2px 2px rgba(95,108,135,.18); } .ds-installation-recess { width: 544px; height: 164px; border-radius: 82px; background: #E6EAF1; box-shadow: inset 5px 7px 10px rgba(143,155,177,.40), inset -5px -6px 8px rgba(255,255,255,.95); }

narrative.overview: The app icon's silver capsule holds the app and its Applications destination. The outlined Airdraft wordmark introduces the window; the arrow and two short instructions explain the action. Finder owns the files, labels, selection and drag interaction.
dos: Do inspect the mounted Finder window, including retained path and status bars.
Do regenerate artwork from code and preserve its provenance file.
Do keep native labels and installation behavior intact.
donts: Don't add FinderInfo to the signed app to hide its extension; strict signing rejects it.
Don't claim a local preview is a published release.
